claims.text: Bulk configurational-entropy and sluggish-diffusion models predict intrinsic thermal stability in nearly equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
Five-component transition-metal high-entropy alloy nanoparticles will undergo rapid phase separation or ordering at elevated temperatures.
Surface-energy minimization and enhanced surface diffusion override bulk thermodynamic and kinetic stability constraints in these nanoparticles.
NbTaTiV can exist as a single-phase solid solution.
CoCrFeMnNi nanoparticles can be prepared in a single-phase solid-solution state.
Annealing should be performed at 500–900°C or 0.5–0.7 Tm for 1–100 hours.
A particle-size range of 5–50 nm maximizes surface effects.
Increasing surface-to-volume ratio reduces the effective configurational-entropy barrier per atom.
Surface diffusion coefficients in high-entropy alloy nanoparticles exceed the effective diffusion rates associated with bulk sluggish-diffusion behavior.
High configurational entropy stabilizes bulk single-phase HEAs, while sluggish diffusion kinetically inhibits precipitation.
Reduced atomic coordination at nanoparticle surfaces lowers the energy penalty for local ordering or phase separation.
Nanoparticle surfaces act as defect sinks and rapid mass-transport pathways that bypass bulk sluggish-diffusion barriers.
Surface-driven evolution will produce lower-surface-energy core-shell segregation or surface ordering rather than preserving a random solid solution.
Chemical short-range order and ordered clusters can evolve in an equiatomic refractory high-entropy alloy.
Nanoparticles will segregate or order at temperatures where bulk samples of identical composition remain single-phase.
Structural evolution in the nanoparticles will be orders of magnitude faster than in bulk samples.
Bulk NbTaTiV remains a single BCC solid solution up to 900°C.
Single-phase Al0.1CoCrFeNi exhibits no irradiation-induced precipitates up to approximately 43 dpa at room temperature.
Surface-driven instability applies below 100 nm, whereas particles above about 200 nm behave like stable bulk material because surface effects become negligible.
Extremely high mixing enthalpy can favor ordering regardless of particle size.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis is framed around five-component alloys, but NbTaTiV is repeatedly used as an example and experimental test material even though it contains only four elements.

The boundary states that hypothesis failure means bulk stability holds, but also lists alloys that favor ordering regardless of size; size-independent ordering is instability rather than restoration of bulk single-phase stability.
